_comment: Expectations for railbank_readorder_matrix.c (bd xdu2.10, Track A), read by run_railbank_dynamic_matrix.py. Rows 1,3,11,12,13 declined 'array has cells no iteration writes' on the pre-change oracle (cq-opt sha256 c6f61f80...) and accept now; row 2 accepted on both (its early return already makes n > 0 dominate, so -O1 emits no per-loop guard); rows 5,7-10,14 are unsound neighbours that must keep the C6 decline. Row 6 (partial write) moved from the C6 string to the classical-mux string: that is the string its EXPLICIT-GUARD twin already declines with on the oracle, because a partial write is the promoter's (C7) business, not C6's. The 'pins' field (ignored by the runner) says which C6 sub-clause each decline row exercises: the diagnostic string is shared by six sub-clauses, so the runner cannot tell them apart; the lit fixtures railbank_readorder_reject_* carry the CQ_CTRL_DBG read-order anchor that does (Rule-13 round 1, P3-4).

1.stage1_note: clang -O1 no longer emits two separate n > 0 loop guards; the row no longer exercises the non-dominated read

3.stage1_note: clang -O1 no longer emits two separate n > 0 loop guards around the large body

5._note: bd 01po.19 S4 (merge a3fbac74): DECLINE->ACCEPT (row 3 of the dynamic matrix, unguarded). The read-order anchor no longer runs on this route: the window pre-mints every cell at its entry. Reviewed 2026-10-15 (bd 01po.19.21).
5.pins: (pre-S4 decline) NOT read order: the read-loop SCEV trip clause (n-1 != extent); no read-order anchor. Neighbour copy of shared row 3.

6.diagnostic: cq taint escape: tainted value muxed by a classical-condition phi
6.pins: NOT read order: the promoter/C7 partial-write wall (the string its explicit-guard twin gives on the oracle).

7._note: bd 01po.19 S4 (merge a3fbac74): DECLINE->ACCEPT (row 5 of the dynamic matrix, unguarded). Never-written cells are pre-minted |0> window rails, a valid refinement of C's indeterminate value (owner ruling D1: uninit == zero-init bank). Trace argv a b: 3 of 5 cells rotated, 5 measured. Reviewed 2026-10-15 (bd 01po.19.21).
7.pins: (pre-S4 decline) NOT read order: the early-exit write loop fails C6's single-exiting-block/exact-BTC conjunct before any read is asked; no anchor.

8._note: bd 01po.19 S4 (merge a3fbac74): DECLINE->ACCEPT. The k==0 bypass reads pre-minted |0> rails (IR read: window minted before the `k != 0 && n > 0` guard). Never-written cells are pre-minted |0> window rails, a valid refinement of C's indeterminate value (owner ruling D1: uninit == zero-init bank). Reviewed 2026-10-15 (bd 01po.19.21).
8.pins: (pre-S4 decline) READ ORDER (anchor fires): the bypass under unrelated k is unrefuted. With 9 and 14, the rows mutant M1 flips.

9._note: bd 01po.19 S4 (merge a3fbac74): DECLINE->ACCEPT. For n in 1..2 the guard-false edge reads pre-minted |0> rails. Never-written cells are pre-minted |0> window rails, a valid refinement of C's indeterminate value (owner ruling D1: uninit == zero-init bank). Reviewed 2026-10-15 (bd 01po.19.21).
9.pins: (pre-S4 decline) READ ORDER (anchor fires): write guard n>2 does not refute read guard n>0.

10._note: ACCEPT by ruling 2026-10-15 (bd 01po.19.21, bd memory ruling-red-heavy-tests-2026-10-15). The verdict is a compile-time property, independent of argv; the driver is now the DEFINED slice(argc + 1, argc) (m = n - 1, the read bound still another variable). Trace argv a b: 4 window rails, 4 Ry, 3 measured. HISTORY: the driver was slice(argc, argc + 1), undefined on every run; since bd 01po.19 S4 (merge a3fbac74) that also accepted, and its lowered read loaded the word past `%.rails` and measured it as a handle (trace argv a b: h0 measured twice). A provably out-of-bounds window read should fail loudly: bd 01po.24.
10.pins: (pre-S4 decline) READ ORDER (anchor fires) AND the read-loop SCEV trip clause (m != n): doubly fenced, so M1 leaves it declining.

14._note: bd 01po.19 S4 (merge a3fbac74): DECLINE->ACCEPT. The unrefuted n<0 edge is a negative VLA extent, undefined in C, so the defined executions (n>0) read only written cells. Reviewed 2026-10-15 (bd 01po.19.21).
14.pins: (pre-S4 decline) READ ORDER (anchor fires): read guard n != 0 is not refuted by n <= 0.

15.pins: Round-3 F-1: a read after a fully-merged tainted diamond is NOT in its region; RED on 928eb206.

16.pins: Hand-unrolled twin of 15 (argv a b, n=2).

17.pins: Round-3 F-1, fixed bank, diamond before the write; RED on 928eb206.

18.pins: Round-3 F-1, fixed bank, diamond between write and read; RED on 928eb206.
